newsitem.title: UK: Nationwide - UK house prices up 1.2 percent in May.
newsitem.headline: Nationwide - UK house prices up 1.2 percent in May.

text.p: Britain's housing market recovery picked up pace in May with prices rising by 1.2 percent over the month, the Nationwide Building Society said on Friday.
That left prices 10 percent higher year-on-year and followed a 0.4 percent increase in April. HOUSE PRICES (index base Q1 1983=100) MAY APRIL MAY 96

"The apparent strength of price increases over recent months contrasts with the more subdued picture of market activity indicated by recent mortgage lending data," said Paul Sanderson, Nationwide's head of research.

"This suggests shortages of property for sale remain an important feature of the market, particularly in London and parts of the South East, where the sharpest price rises are still heavily concentrated," he said.
Sanderson said the housing market remains well underpinned by solid personal incomes growth, falling unemployment and "excellent affordability."
But despite recent gains, prices nationally remain about 25 percent below their long-term trend in real terms and sales are running at only two-thirds of their late 1980s peak.

With the housing market not affecting the overall economy as homeowners are not borrowing heavily against their properties to finance consumer spending, Sanderson said the wisdom of cutting mortgage interest tax relief was questionable.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown is due to hold a budget within the next month or so and is widely tipped to reduce MIRAS, or possibly even axe it altogether.

"The timing of such a move might be questionable, however, given the limited strength of the recovery, prospects of a further increase in interest rates and the disproportionate regional impact of reductions in tax relief," Sanderson said.
He said cuts would hit hardest in the north where the market is relatively subdued.
